description: Fix trade frequency bottleneck. Current scheduler runs MCL then MNQ sequentially and only on 1h timeframe, generating ~1-2 signals/day total. Need 2 trades/day to hit 60-trade gate. Solution: parallel symbol scanning + 15m timeframe at half position size.

userStories.title: Parallelize MCL + MNQ scanner jobs (run concurrently, not sequentially)
userStories.description: As a trader, I want MCL and MNQ scanned simultaneously so that both instruments can generate signals in the same market open window.
acceptanceCriteria: engine/main.py market_open_scan_job uses asyncio.gather() for 1h scans
Both MCL and MNQ symbols scan in parallel (not sequential await)
Each symbol's result is logged independently with [MARKET_OPEN] prefix
If one symbol fails, the other still completes
ruff check on modified files passes
userStories.notes: Implementation: engine/main.py lines 649-753. Uses asyncio.gather() to run _scan_1h tasks in parallel. Each scan logs independently. Non-blocking error handling ensures one failure doesn't halt others.

userStories.title: Add 15-minute timeframe scan to market_open_scan job
userStories.description: As a trader, I want a 15m STC scan to run alongside the 1h scan so that faster timeframe signals increase trade frequency toward the 60-trade gate.
acceptanceCriteria: engine/main.py market_open_scan_job fires 15m scans for MCL and MNQ in addition to 1h
15m signals include timeframe='15m' in signal metadata
1h signals include timeframe='1h' in signal metadata
15m and 1h scans all run concurrently via asyncio.gather() (4 tasks total)
Engine logs distinguish 15m vs 1h signals ([MARKET_OPEN] prefix)
ruff check on modified files passes
userStories.notes: Implementation: engine/main.py _scan_15m() function using BacktestDataLoader + signal generation for speed. TechnicalReport already includes timeframe field which flows to signal metadata through pipeline. Position sizing handled at trade approval layer based on signal timeframe.

userStories.title: Add signal_timeframe to pending_trade_approvals and trade_journal tables
userStories.description: As a trader, I want to know which timeframe generated each trade so I can compare 1h vs 15m performance over the 30-day validation window.
acceptanceCriteria: pipeline_router extracts timeframe from technical_report and passes to insert_pending_approval()
approval_router extracts timeframe from pipeline_snapshot and passes to add_journal_entry()
Migration runs clean on engine/data/jarvis_trader.db (idempotent ALTER TABLE)
userStories.notes: Implementation: migration_014 adds timeframe TEXT (nullable) to both tables. _mixins_pending_approvals.py updated to accept timeframe param. _mixins_journal.py updated to accept timeframe param. pipeline_router extracts from technical_report.timeframe. approval_router enriches journal with timeframe. Data flows: Pipeline → TechnicalReport.timeframe → analyst_reports → pipeline_snapshot → approval_router → journal_entry.
